REVISIONS IN THIS VERSION:
1. Forage fish (Sand Lance, Atlantic Herring, Capelin) are NO LONGER excluded
   from matchBiomasses() — they are calibrated like every other species.
2. reproduction_level (setBevertonHolt) is now set ONCE, in a single place,
   after growth + biomass have been iterated to a stable shape, and BEFORE
   the final matchYield/catchability calibration loop. Previously this was
   set twice (0.8, then 0.5) in two different chunks with conflicting
   in-code comments — that ambiguity is removed.
3. A yield-vs-F dome-shape check is run both immediately after setting
   reproduction_level AND again after the final matchYield loop, since
   matchYield/matchBiomasses can shift SSB enough to alter the *effective*
   reproduction level even without calling setBevertonHolt again.

Workflow order:
  calibrateBiomass (kappa, coarse total biomass)
    -> iterate matchBiomasses + matchGrowth until stable (size structure, growth)
    -> set reproduction_level ONCE (density-dependence, on stable size structure)
    -> check yield-vs-F dome shape
    -> seal catchability tuning (predation, independent of fishing gears)
    -> iterate matchYieldCustom + matchBiomasses (fishing catchability, final biomass polish)
    -> re-check yield-vs-F dome shape (catch divergence if matchYield distorted it)

Read in DFO Summer RV survey abundance and biomass data from DFO Maritimes region data team, subset depth strata to include only 4VsW (in line with Bundy et al. EwE spatial domain).

Calculate the minimum length and weight cutoffs from length distributions for us in model, to account for the fact that smaller sizes not selected by the RV gear. Maybe should add a maximum length and weight as well.
```{r}
stat <- read.csv("Ess_data/LF_Biomass_Abund.csv")

# ── LOOKUP: RAW SURVEY NAME -> MODEL NAME ────────────────────────────────────
species_code_lookup <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"             = "Atlantic Cod",
  "HADDOCK"                   = "Haddock",
  "WHITE HAKE"                = "White Hake",
  "SILVER HAKE"               = "Silver Hake",
  "POLLOCK"                   = "Pollock",
  "REDFISH UNSEPARATED"       = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"           = "American Plaice",
  "YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"       = "Yellowtail Flounder",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"             = "Spiny Dogfish",
  "HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Halibut",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"      = "Red Hake",
  "MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER" = "Monkfish",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"       = "Sand Lance",
  "WITCH FLOUNDER"            = "Witch Flounder",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"         = "Atlantic Herring",
  "THORNY SKATE"              = "Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"              = "Winter Skate",
  "LONGHORN SCULPIN"          = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "CAPELIN"                   = "Capelin")


# Species lookup
stat2 <- stat |>
  filter(YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) |>
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) |>
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) |>  # 4VsW only
  select(
    depth_strata = STRAT,
    year = YEAR,
    species_name_raw = COMMON_NAME,
    length_cm = FLEN,
    abundance = Abundance_Strata) |>
  mutate(
    length_cm = ifelse(
      species_name_raw == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)", # herring looks like measured in mm!
      length_cm / 10,
      length_cm),
    species_name = species_code_lookup[species_name_raw]) |>
  filter(!is.na(species_name))

# 1. Sum abundance across depth strata by species, year and length
lf_year_length <- stat2 %>%
  group_by(species_name, year, length_cm) %>%
  summarise(
    abundance = sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")


weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs = 0.05) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  x <- x[ok]
  w <- w[ok]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)

  o <- order(x)
  x <- x[o]
  w <- w[o]

  cw <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  x[which(cw >= probs)[1]]
}

annual_length_quantiles <- lf_year_length %>%
  group_by(species_name, year) %>%
  summarise(
    q01_length_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, abundance, 0.01),
    q05_length_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, abundance, 0.05),
    q50_length_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, abundance, 0.50),
    .groups = "drop")

cutoff_quantile_summary <- annual_length_quantiles %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  summarise(
    cutoff_q01_median = median(q01_length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    cutoff_q01_q75 = quantile(q01_length_cm, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    cutoff_q05_median = median(q05_length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

cutoff_quantile_summary

# Overall abundance-weighted length distributions
lf_overall <- lf_year_length %>%
  mutate(
    length_bin = floor(length_cm / 2) * 2
  )%>%
  group_by(species_name, length_bin) %>%
  summarise(
    abundance = sum(abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_name), !is.na(length_bin), abundance > 0)

# Optional: derive thresholds from q05_q75
length_thresholds <- cutoff_quantile_summary %>%
  transmute(
    species_name,
    threshold_cm = cutoff_q01_q75)



# Plot
ggplot(lf_overall, aes(x = length_bin, y = abundance)) +
  geom_col(width = 1.8) +
  geom_vline(
    data = length_thresholds,
    aes(xintercept = threshold_cm),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.6 ) +
  facet_wrap(~species_name, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Length (cm)",
    y = "Total stratified abundance",
    title = "Abundance-weighted length distributions across all years and strata",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines show q75 of annual abundance-weighted 5th percentile length")



# ── LOWER SIZE CUTOFF FOR ESTIMATING BIOMASS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
biomass_cutoff <- cutoff_quantile_summary |>
  left_join(
    external_species_info |>
      select(species, a, b),
    by = c("species_name" = "species")) |>
  mutate(
    biomass_cutoff = round(a * cutoff_q01_q75 ^ b, 1)) |>
  select(
    species = species_name,
    biomass_cutoff)

# ── JOIN BACK TO SPECIES INFO ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
external_species_info <- external_species_info |>
  left_join(
    biomass_cutoff,
    by = "species")


# CHeck if need to adjust max_w for some species (too small max_w from RFishBase)

# Survey maximum lengths
survey_max_lengths <- stat2 %>%
  group_by(species_name) %>%
  summarise(
    survey_max_length_cm = max(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),
    q99_length_cm = weighted_quantile(length_cm, abundance, 0.99),
    .groups = "drop")

# Convert FishBase max lengths to max weights using W = aL^b
max_weight_comparison <- survey_max_lengths %>%
  left_join(
    external_species_info %>% select(species, a, b, w_max),
    by = c("species_name" = "species")) %>%
  mutate(
    survey_max_weight_g = a * survey_max_length_cm ^ b,
    biomass_cutoffHigh = a * q99_length_cm ^ b,
    w_max_ratio = survey_max_weight_g / w_max, # survey max w, proportion of model w_max, should be less than 1
    q99_ratio =  biomass_cutoffHigh / w_max  #99th percentile of max weights, should be less than 1
  )

max_weight_comparison 
max_weight_comparison <- max_weight_comparison |> select(species = species_name, biomass_cutoffHigh  )


# ── JOIN BACK TO SPECIES INFO ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
external_species_info <- external_species_info |> left_join(max_weight_comparison, by = "species" )


```

Copy species life history parameters into the species parameters for the model
```{r}
external_species_info <-select(external_species_info,c("species","w_max","w_mat", "w_min","beta" ,"sigma" ,"a","b","age_mat","R_max" , "biomass_cutoff", "biomass_cutoffHigh"))

# Correct w_min for oviparous skates — hatchlings emerge at ~10 cm TL (~5 g),
# so w_min = 0.001 g creates phantom size classes that inflate predation mortality
# and drive erepro > 1. Verified: a * 10^b gives ~4.6 g (Winter) and ~5.6 g (Thorny).
external_species_info$w_min[external_species_info$species == "Winter Skate"] <- 5
external_species_info$w_min[external_species_info$species == "Thorny Skate"] <- 5

# ── PPMR (beta) corrections for piscivores ───────────────────────────────────
# beta values are now biomass-weighted mean PPMR from 00_EZ_SpeciesParams_extraction.R
# (weighted.mean(ppmr, w = prey_wght)), so large fish prey dominate rather than
# numerically abundant tiny prey. No manual overrides needed.

```

```{r}
# Recalculate total annual biomass from raw survey data, 4VsW strata (443-466)
# Replaces pre-processed DFO_Biomass_selected_species.csv for strata consistency
biomass_obs <- stat %>%
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466,
         YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 2024) %>%
  mutate(species_name = species_code_lookup[COMMON_NAME]) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_name)) %>%
  group_by(Year = YEAR, species_name) %>%
  summarise(biomass_g = sum(Biomass_Strata_KG, na.rm = TRUE) * 1e3, .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = species_name, values_from = biomass_g, values_fill = 0) %>%
  select(Year, any_of(species_order))
biomass_obs[is.na(biomass_obs)] <- 0

## FORAGE FISH CATCHABILITY ASSUMPTION: scale up biomass herring X 50 , sandeel, and capelin by factor of 200 - TEST SENSITIVITY OF RUNS, based approximately on Harly et al. 2001 and Bundy et al.
biomass_obs <- biomass_obs %>%
  mutate(`Atlantic Herring` = `Atlantic Herring` * 50,
    `Sand Lance` = `Sand Lance` * 200,
    `Capelin` = `Capelin` * 200)

```

To intialise model need to time-average biomasses between 1978 and 1985 (prior to any detectable trends in species, relatively more stable period)

```{r}
library(reshape2)
#Aggregate observed biomass to mean biomass
biomass_obs_sub <- subset(biomass_obs, Year >= 1978 & Year <= 2024)
biomass_ts <- reshape2::melt(biomass_obs_sub, id.vars = 1)
names(biomass_ts)<-c("Year","Species","Biomass")
saveRDS(biomass_ts, "Ess_data/biomass_ts.RDS") 
## Arithmetic mean
# mean_biomass_obs <- subset(biomass_ts, Year<=max(years_to_use))%>%
#   group_by(Species)%>% summarise(biomass_observed =mean(Biomass,  na.rm = T))
## Geom mean
mean_biomass_obs <- subset(biomass_ts, Year <= max(years_to_use)) %>%
  group_by(Species) %>% summarise( biomass_observed = exp(mean(log(Biomass[Biomass > 0]), na.rm = TRUE)))

mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed<- ifelse(is.nan( mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed),NA,  mean_biomass_obs$biomass_observed)
```

```{r}
fishing_type <- read.csv("Ess_data/new.gear_params.csv")
names(fishing_type)[1] <- "species"

new_seal <- read.csv("Ess_data/seal_gear_params.csv")

#new_seal$catchability <- new_seal$catchability / 10   # Reduce initial seal catchability

# Gaussian size-selectivity function (used by mizer internally)
gaussian_sizeweight <- function(w, species_params, w_opt, sigma, ...) {
  exp(-0.5 * ((log(w) - log(w_opt)) / sigma)^2)
}

rownames(fishing_type) <- paste(fishing_type$species, fishing_type$gear, sep = ", ")
rownames(new_seal)     <- paste(new_seal$species,     new_seal$gear,     sep = ", ")
updated_gp <- bind_rows(fishing_type, new_seal)
```

## Set Initial Fishing Effort
## Read the fishing history data/set fishing into params from NAFO
## set intial effort as mean_effort - SEALS MISSING

```{r fishing-effort}

effort_full       <- read.csv("Ess_data/effort_gear_with_seals.csv", row.names = 1)
effort_full$Year  <- as.numeric(rownames(effort_full))

gear_cols <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic", "Seals")

# Max computed on the FULL series (from 1970) since that's the true historical max,
# not just the >=1978 subset you'll actually use for the model period
max_by_gear <- apply(effort_full[, gear_cols], 2, max, na.rm = TRUE)

# Subset to modelled period (1978 onwards)
effort_final <- subset(effort_full, Year >= 1978)

# Rescale relative effort using the FULL-series max, applied to the subset
effort_final[, gear_cols] <- sweep(effort_final[, gear_cols], 2, max_by_gear, FUN = "/")

# Confirm scaling - max may now be < 1 within the subset if true historical
# peak occurred before 1978
range(effort_final[, gear_cols])

mean_effort <- colMeans(effort_final[effort_final$Year %in% years_to_use, gear_cols])

# Select only the fishing gears (exclude Seals if initial_effort should only
# cover the 4 fishing gears used in newMultispeciesParams)
initial_effort <- mean_effort[c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic","Seals")]
```

Set up params then
set up initial catchability using this mean relative effort and catchability of 1 as initial value only - BUT WILL ESTIMATE LATER

```{r}
params <- newMultispeciesParams(external_species_info,interaction = NULL, resource_dynamics = "resource_semichemostat",kappa = 1e11, resource_rate = 10, w_pp_cutoff = 100,gear_params = updated_gp,initial_effort = initial_effort)


# ── z0 CHECK: background mortality ───────────────────────────────────────────
sp <- species_params(params)
print(sp[, intersect(c("species", "w_mat", "w_max", "z0", "z0pre", "erepro"), names(sp))])

# Override z0pre after inspecting: high ext_mort_at_wmat for slow-growing species
```

```{r interaction-matrix}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 4VsW MULTISPECIES INTERACTION MATRIX
# Schoener's D spatial overlap used directly as θ_ij (habitat encounter prob.)
# Strata 443–466 | 19 species | Cook & Bundy 2010
# Strata 440–442 are NAFO 4Vn (northeastern shelf) — excluded.
# Stratum 443 confirmed as 4Vs — included.
# Strata 434–439 are inshore/edge (very low biomass) — excluded.
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

library(tidyverse)
library(factoextra)

# ── 1. STRATA VERIFICATION ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
stat$strat_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(stat$STRAT)))

strat_biomass <- aggregate(Biomass_Strata_KG ~ strat_num,
                           data = stat[!is.na(stat$strat_num), ], sum, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Strata included (443-466, 4VsW domain) and their total biomass (kg):\n")
print(strat_biomass[strat_biomass$strat_num >= 443 & strat_biomass$strat_num <= 466, ])
cat("\nExcluded strata 440-442 (NAFO 4Vn — northeastern shelf, outside model domain):\n")
print(strat_biomass[strat_biomass$strat_num %in% 440:442, ])

# ── 2. NAME MAP: raw survey name → model species name ────────────────────────
name_map <- c(
  "COD(ATLANTIC)"              = "Atlantic Cod",
  "HADDOCK"                    = "Haddock",
  "REDFISH UNSEPARATED"        = "Redfish Unseparated",
  "AMERICAN PLAICE"            = "American Plaice",
  "SILVER HAKE"                = "Silver Hake",
  "MONKFISH,GOOSEFISH,ANGLER"  = "Monkfish",
  "WHITE HAKE"                 = "White Hake",
  "THORNY SKATE"               = "Thorny Skate",
  "WINTER SKATE"               = "Winter Skate",
  "POLLOCK"                    = "Pollock",
  "YELLOWTAIL FLOUNDER"        = "Yellowtail Flounder",
  "LONGHORN SCULPIN"           = "Longhorn Sculpin",
  "SQUIRREL OR RED HAKE"       = "Red Hake",
  "HERRING(ATLANTIC)"          = "Atlantic Herring",
  "NORTHERN SAND LANCE"        = "Sand Lance",
  "SPINY DOGFISH"              = "Spiny Dogfish",
  "HALIBUT(ATLANTIC)"          = "Atlantic Halibut",
  "CAPELIN"                    = "Capelin",
  "WITCH FLOUNDER"             = "Witch Flounder"
)

# ── 3. BUILD STRATUM × SPECIES BIOMASS MATRIX ────────────────────────────────
stratum_matrix <- stat %>%
  filter(COMMON_NAME %in% names(name_map)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) %>%
  group_by(strat_num, COMMON_NAME) %>%
  summarise(biomass = sum(Biomass_Strata_KG, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = COMMON_NAME, values_from = biomass, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("strat_num")

# Check all 19 species present
missing_spp <- setdiff(names(name_map), colnames(stratum_matrix))
if (length(missing_spp) > 0) warning("Missing from stratum matrix: ", paste(missing_spp, collapse = ", "))

# ── 4. SCHOENER'S D ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
col_sums <- colSums(stratum_matrix)
col_sums[col_sums == 0] <- 1
dist_norm      <- sweep(stratum_matrix, 2, col_sums, "/")
schoener_raw   <- 1 - (as.matrix(dist(t(dist_norm), method = "manhattan")) / 2)
diag(schoener_raw) <- 0.2

# Map to model names and reorder to match params species order
colnames(schoener_raw) <- name_map[colnames(schoener_raw)]
rownames(schoener_raw) <- name_map[rownames(schoener_raw)]
sp_order     <- species_params(params)$species
schoener_D   <- schoener_raw[sp_order, sp_order]

cat("\nSchoener's D matrix (strata 443-466):\n")
print(round(schoener_D, 2))

# ── 5. CLUSTERING & DENDROGRAM ───────────────────────────────────────────────
d   <- as.dist(1 - schoener_D)
fit <- hclust(d, method = "ward.D2")

plot(fit,
     main = "4VsW Species Co-occurrence (Strata 443-466)",
     sub  = "Schoener's D | Ward.D2",
     xlab = "", ylab = "Ecological distance", hang = -1)
abline(h = 0.5, col = "red", lty = 2)
rect.hclust(fit, h = 0.5, border = "blue")

fviz_dend(fit, h = 0.5, type = "rectangle", rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE,
          k_colors = "jco", cex = 0.6,
          main = "4VsW Ecological Guilds — Strata 443-466")

clusters <- cutree(fit, h = 0.5)
cat("\nGuild assignments (h = 0.5):\n")
print(sort(clusters))

# ── 6. INTERACTION MATRIX — scaled Schoener's D (4VsW depth-stratum overlap) ─
# θ_ij in mizer scales encounter rates between predator i and prey j.
# Schoener's D is ecologically appropriate here: it measures spatial co-occurrence
# (i.e. whether species share habitat and can encounter each other), which is
# the correct biological basis for θ_ij — diet composition (Cook & Bundy) captures
# what is eaten after an encounter, which is already handled by the feeding kernel.
# Raw D values (0.4–0.9) cause predation overload when used directly; scaling by
# 0.3 brings co-occurring pairs to θ ~0.12–0.27 while preserving 4VsW structure.
# Diagonal (intraspecific) set to 0.3 independently.
inter <- schoener_D * 0.3
diag(inter) <- 0.3

# Elasmobranchs rarely consumed — defended by spines/size; scale down as prey
inter[, "Spiny Dogfish"]  <- inter[, "Spiny Dogfish"]  * 0.3
inter[, "Thorny Skate"]   <- inter[, "Thorny Skate"]   * 0.5
inter[, "Winter Skate"]   <- inter[, "Winter Skate"]   * 0.5

# ── Cook & Bundy column overrides (diet data > spatial overlap for these prey) ─

# Sand Lance: dominant prey for flatfish & Haddock in C&B but beta too high for
# their feeding kernel to reach sand lance size — boost column to compensate
inter["Haddock",             "Sand Lance"] <- 0.60
inter["American Plaice",     "Sand Lance"] <- 0.70
inter["Yellowtail Flounder", "Sand Lance"] <- 0.70
inter["Witch Flounder",      "Sand Lance"] <- 0.40
inter["Longhorn Sculpin",    "Sand Lance"] <- 0.50
inter["Atlantic Cod",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.50
inter["Thorny Skate",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.60
inter["Winter Skate",        "Sand Lance"] <- 0.40

# Atlantic Herring: C&B dominant prey for true piscivores only
# White Hake 34.46%, Cod 18.31%, Pollock/Dogfish/Monkfish heuristic
inter["White Hake",      "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.60
inter["Spiny Dogfish",   "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.50
inter["Pollock",         "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.55
inter["Monkfish",        "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.50
inter["Atlantic Cod",    "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.60

# Invertivores: C&B shows Herring is negligible — cap low so Schoener's D
# base value doesn't inflate Herring predation for these species
# Haddock 0.07%, American Plaice 0%, Yellowtail Flounder 0.05%,
# Witch Flounder ~0%, Longhorn Sculpin ~0%
inter["Haddock",             "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["American Plaice",     "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Yellowtail Flounder", "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Witch Flounder",      "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05
inter["Longhorn Sculpin",    "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.05

# American Plaice: model over-predates; C&B shows mainly Thorny Skate eating it
inter[, "American Plaice"] <- inter[, "American Plaice"] * 0.3
inter["Thorny Skate", "American Plaice"] <- 0.50   # restore Thorny Skate (C&B dominant)

# Forage fish do not eat each other — zero out Herring↔Capelin cross-predation
inter["Atlantic Herring", "Capelin"]     <- 0.0
inter["Capelin",          "Atlantic Herring"] <- 0.0

params <- setInteraction(params, interaction = inter)

cat("\nInteraction matrix (scaled Schoener's D × 0.3):\n")
print(round(interaction_matrix(params), 2))
```

## STEP 1: Calibrate Biomass Scale (coarse, total-community kappa)

```{r calibrate-biomass}
params <- params |> calibrateBiomass() |> steady()
plotlySpectra(params, power = 2)
plotlyFeedingLevel(params)
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params)

# check new kappa
resource_params(params)

```


## STEP 2: Iterate matchBiomasses + matchGrowth until stable
All species, including forage fish (Sand Lance, Atlantic Herring, Capelin), are
matched together. They are NOT excluded — their inflated biomass_observed
(catchability-corrected x50/x200) is treated as the real calibration target,
the same as every other species. If kappa/resource_rate can't support that
target, that is a signal to revisit the resource parameters (kappa, r_pp) or
the catchability-correction factors themselves, not to quietly exclude the
species from calibration.

Order within each iteration: matchBiomasses first (gets n0/size-structure
toward target), then matchGrowth (gamma adjusted to match von Bertalanffy
growth on that structure), then steady(). Guard against matchGrowth driving
any species' RDI to 0.
```{r}
for (i in 1:25) {
  params <- params |> matchBiomasses() |> steady()

  params_test <- tryCatch(matchGrowth(params), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(params_test)) {
    rdi <- getRDI(params_test)
    bad <- names(rdi)[rdi == 0]
    if (length(bad) == 0) {
      params <- params_test
    } else {
      warning("matchGrowth iteration ", i, ": RDI = 0 for ",
              paste(bad, collapse = ", "), " — skipping matchGrowth this step")
    }
  } else {
    warning("matchGrowth failed at iteration ", i, " — skipping")
  }
  params <- steady(params)
}

plotlyFeedingLevel(params)
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params, ratio = TRUE)
plotGrowthCurves(params, species_panel = TRUE)
```

could use to the below plot instead to check ratio is within +/- 1.2 model biomass/observed biomass for all species (I stopped when Total Relative Error was 0.385)
```{r}

# Wrapper: exclude specified gears (default "Seals") from model yield before comparing to
# observed NAFO catches. Seals are parameterised as a gear but represent external predation,
# not commercial catch — including them inflates modelled yield per species.
plotYieldExcl <- function(params, exclude_gear = "Seals", ...) {
  gp <- gear_params(params)
  gear_params(params) <- gp[!gp$gear %in% exclude_gear, ]
  plotYieldObservedVsModel(params, ...)
}

# Wrapper: exclude Seals gear from Fmort plot. Seals are added as a gear for
# convenience but their mortality is predation, not fishing — including them
# conflates fishing F with predation M in the diagnostic plot.
plotFMortExcl <- function(params, exclude_gear = "Seals", ...) {
  gp <- gear_params(params)
  gear_params(params) <- gp[!gp$gear %in% exclude_gear, ]
  plotlyFMort(params, ...)
}

# Plot comparison of model-predicted vs observed yield (catch) — seals excluded

# Plot interactive feeding level by size for each species

plotlyFeedingLevel(params)

# which species have unrealistic reproduction:

species_params(params)[which(species_params(params)$erepro > 1),]$species
```      

## STEP 3: Set reproduction_level ONCE, on the now-stable growth/biomass structure

This is set in exactly one place in the script (previously it was set twice,
in two different chunks, with conflicting values — 0.8 then 0.5 — leaving it
ambiguous which value actually governed the final catchability calibration).
It is set here because:
  - growth (gamma) is now matched, so size-at-maturity timing (and therefore
    spawning stock biomass, which reproduction_level is computed relative to)
    is realistic
  - biomass/size-structure (n0) is now roughly matched, so SSB itself is in
    the right ballpark
  - it is set BEFORE matchYield/catchability calibration, so that fishing
    mortality is calibrated against a stock-recruit relationship that won't
    change again afterward except via the biomass shifts matchYield itself
    causes (checked again at the end of Step 4 below)

rl = 0.7 gives dome-shaped yield-vs-F curves peaking at realistic F levels in
testing. Values closer to 1 -> peak at very low F (fragile stock); values
closer to 0 -> no compensation, no dome.
```{r}
params <- setBevertonHolt(params, reproduction_level = 0.7)
params <- steady(params)

# Check dome shape immediately, before any further calibration steps run
plotYieldVsF(params, species = "Atlantic Cod")
plotYieldVsF(params, species = "Spiny Dogfish")

# which species have unrealistic reproduction (erepro > 1) after this step:
species_params(params)[which(species_params(params)$erepro > 1), ]$species
```

## SEAL CATCHABILITY TUNING
Independent of fishing-gear calibration — seal consumption is set to match an
external QB-based target, not observed catch. Run after reproduction_level is
set (Step 3) and before final matchYield/catchability calibration (Step 4), so
that fishing catchability is calibrated against a model that already includes
realistic seal predation pressure.

Per-species catchability SPLIT is set from real diet data (no per-species
consumption data exists, only the total QB target) — averaged and normalised
from two independent 1980-1985-era sources:
  - ESS Tech Report (CDEENA), Table 2a, Diet 3: grey seal diet 1980-1985,
    built from Benoit & Bowen (1990) mainland Scotian Shelf fecal samples,
    converted from % occurrence to % weight and normalised.
  - Bowen & Harrison (1994): offshore (Sable Island) grey seal diet, July
    1991 - January 1993, % wet weight from otolith/hard-part recovery.
Different foraging grounds (mainland vs offshore), same era — averaging is a
pragmatic compromise across two legitimate, citable, period-appropriate
sources, not a statistically rigorous pooling. Flag this in any writeup.
```{r}
# ── Source 1: ESS Tech Report Table 2a, Diet 3 (1980-1985, Benoit & Bowen 1990) ──
ess_8085_pct <- c(
  "Atlantic Cod"         = 2.1 + 19.1,  # Large Cod + Small Cod combined (single Cod species here)
  "Silver Hake"          = 3.1 + 16.1,  # Large + Small Silver Hake combined
  "Haddock"              = 10.6,
  "American Plaice"      = 4.1,
  "Yellowtail Flounder"  = NA,          # part of "Flounders" 2.3 - split below
  "Witch Flounder"       = NA,          # part of "Flounders" 2.3 - split below
  "Sand Lance"           = 12.8,
  "Atlantic Herring"     = 6.7,         # "Small Pelagics"
  "Thorny Skate"         = NA,          # part of "Skates" 4.3 - split below
  "Winter Skate"         = NA           # part of "Skates" 4.3 - split below
)

# Flounders (2.3%) not broken out by species in this source — leave at 0 here,
# filled by Bowen & Harrison source instead
ess_8085_pct["Yellowtail Flounder"] <- 0
ess_8085_pct["Witch Flounder"]      <- 0

# Skates (4.3%) not broken out by species — split evenly Thorny/Winter
ess_8085_pct["Thorny Skate"] <- 4.3 / 2
ess_8085_pct["Winter Skate"] <- 4.3 / 2

# ── Source 2: Bowen & Harrison 1994, Table 3 (offshore, % wet weight, total period) ──
bowen_pct <- c(
  "Sand Lance"           = 80.9,
  "Atlantic Cod"         = 11.0,
  "Silver Hake"          = 2.6,
  "American Plaice"      = 1.4,
  "Redfish Unseparated"  = 1.3,
  "Yellowtail Flounder"  = 1.1,
  "Witch Flounder"       = 0.4,
  "Capelin"              = 0.4,
  "Pollock"              = 0.2,
  "Atlantic Herring"     = 0.2,
  "Haddock"              = 0.1,
  "White Hake"           = 0.1,
  "Red Hake"             = 0.1
)

# ── Normalise each source to sum=1 over the 19 model species, then average ───
all_species <- species_params(params)$species

ess_prop_full <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_species)), all_species)
ess_prop_full[names(ess_8085_pct)] <- ess_8085_pct / 100
ess_prop_full <- ess_prop_full / sum(ess_prop_full)

bowen_prop <- setNames(rep(0, length(all_species)), all_species)
bowen_prop[names(bowen_pct)] <- bowen_pct / 100
bowen_prop <- bowen_prop / sum(bowen_prop)

seal_diet_avg <- (ess_prop_full + bowen_prop) / 2
seal_diet_avg <- seal_diet_avg / sum(seal_diet_avg)

cat("Averaged, normalized 1980-1985 seal diet split (proportion of total consumption):\n")
print(round(sort(seal_diet_avg, decreasing = TRUE), 4))
```

```{r}
# ── SEAL CATCHABILITY TUNING ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
seal_abundance   <- readRDS("Ess_data/seal_abundance_digitised.RDS")
ref_years        <- 1978:1985
ref_n_seals      <- mean(seal_abundance$scotian_mean[seal_abundance$year %in% ref_years]) * 1000

seal_body_mass_g       <- 170 * 1000    # confirmed: Bundy 2004 Scotian Shelf EwE
total_biomass_g        <- ref_n_seals * seal_body_mass_g
QB_seal                <- 12.98         # confirmed: Bundy 2004 Table A (Q/B for grey seals)
fish_fraction          <- 0.85          # confirmed: Bowen et al. 1993; DFO grey seal diet
Yield_observed_seals_g <- total_biomass_g * QB_seal * fish_fraction

seal_gear_name <- "Seals"

get_seal_yield <- function(p) {
  sum(sapply(species_params(p)$species, function(sp) {
    n <- initialN(p)[sp, ]
    f <- getFMortGear(p)[seal_gear_name, sp, ]
    sum(f * n * p@w * p@dw)
  }), na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Restore seal catchabilities and scale to QB consumption target.
# Per-species SPLIT now comes from the averaged 1980-1985 diet data above
# (seal_diet_avg), not from new_seal$catchability — this replaces the
# previous unvalidated relative-catchability assumption with real diet
# composition data from Benoit & Bowen (1990) / Bowen & Harrison (1994).
seal_rows <- which(gear_params(params)$gear == seal_gear_name)
seal_gp_species <- gear_params(params)$species[seal_rows]
gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows] <- seal_diet_avg[seal_gp_species]
params <- steady(params)

current_seal_total <- get_seal_yield(params)
scale_factor_seal  <- Yield_observed_seals_g / current_seal_total
gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows] <-
  gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows] * scale_factor_seal
params <- steady(params)
cat("Seal consumption after initial scaling — model/target ratio:",
    round(get_seal_yield(params) / Yield_observed_seals_g, 3), "\n")

```


## STEP 4: matchYieldCustom + matchBiomasses (final catchability + biomass polish)
Now that growth, biomass structure, reproduction_level, and seal predation are
all set, calibrate fishing catchability against observed catch, re-polishing
biomass each iteration. Forage fish remain included throughout — no exclusion.
```{r}
fishing_gears <- c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Small_Mesh", "Pelagic")

# Realistic ceiling on fishing mortality. matchYieldCustom() will happily push
# catchability arbitrarily high to force model yield to match yield_observed,
# even for a species that is biomass-limited that iteration (e.g. mid-way
# through convergence, before matchBiomasses has caught up) — this produces
# F spikes with no stock-assessment basis. Cap apparent F per species/gear
# after each matchYieldCustom call and rescale catchability back down if
# exceeded, rather than trusting the unconstrained fit.
max_F_allowed <- 1.5   # adjust to whatever is biologically defensible for your species set

cap_catchability_to_maxF <- function(params, max_F = max_F_allowed, gears = fishing_gears) {
  gp <- gear_params(params)
  fmort_gear <- getFMortGear(params)  # array: gear x species x size

  for (g in gears) {
    if (!(g %in% dimnames(fmort_gear)[[1]])) next
    peak_F_by_species <- apply(fmort_gear[g, , , drop = FALSE], 2, max, na.rm = TRUE)

    over <- names(peak_F_by_species)[peak_F_by_species > max_F]
    for (sp in over) {
      idx <- which(gp$gear == g & gp$species == sp)
      if (length(idx) == 0) next
      scale_down <- max_F / peak_F_by_species[sp]
      gp$catchability[idx] <- gp$catchability[idx] * scale_down
    }
  }
  gear_params(params) <- gp
  params
}

for (i in 1:20) {
  params <- params |>
    matchYieldCustom(keep = "biomass", gears = fishing_gears) |>
    steady()

  params <- cap_catchability_to_maxF(params)

  params <- params |>
    matchBiomasses() |>
    steady()
}

# Confirm no species/gear exceeds the cap after the loop
fmort_check <- getFMortGear(params)
peak_F_final <- sapply(fishing_gears, function(g) {
  if (g %in% dimnames(fmort_check)[[1]]) apply(fmort_check[g, , , drop = FALSE], 2, max, na.rm = TRUE)
  else NA
})
cat("Peak F by gear x species after capping (should all be <=", max_F_allowed, "):\n")
print(round(peak_F_final, 3))

plotYieldExcl(params, ratio = TRUE)
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params, ratio = TRUE)
plotFMortExcl(params)

# ── Trim seal catchabilities after biomass has shifted ───────────────────────
# Biomass changed during matchYield/matchBiomasses so seal consumption may have
# drifted from QB target — rescale once to correct.
seal_rows_steady <- which(gear_params(params)$gear == seal_gear_name)
current_seal_total <- get_seal_yield(params)
scale_factor_seal  <- Yield_observed_seals_g / current_seal_total
gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows_steady] <-
  gear_params(params)$catchability[seal_rows_steady] * scale_factor_seal
params <- steady(params)
cat("Seal consumption ratio (model/target) after trim:",
    round(get_seal_yield(params) / Yield_observed_seals_g, 3), "\n")

# Final matchBiomass polish after seal trim shifts biomass slightly again
for (i in 1:3) {
  params <- params |> matchBiomasses() |> steady()
}

plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params, ratio = TRUE)
plotYieldExcl(params, ratio = TRUE)
plotFMortExcl(params)

# ── Re-check yield-vs-F dome shape after Step 4 ──────────────────────────────
# matchYield/matchBiomasses can shift SSB enough to alter the EFFECTIVE
# reproduction level even though setBevertonHolt was not called again here.
# If the dome shape has degraded relative to the Step 3 check, a second
# (final) setBevertonHolt pass may be needed — ideally only one extra pass,
# immediately followed by re-running Step 4's final matchBiomasses polish.
plotYieldVsF(params, species = "Atlantic Cod")
plotYieldVsF(params, species = "Spiny Dogfish")

# ── SEAL PREDATION MORTALITY PER SPECIES ─────────────────────────────────────
# Seals are a gear so their mortality appears in getFMortGear, not getM2.
# Compute biomass-weighted mean seal-F per species as a proxy for predation pressure.
# Compare against total M2 (fish predation mortality) to judge relative importance.
seal_fmort_mat <- getFMortGear(params)[seal_gear_name, , ]
biomass_mat    <- sweep(initialN(params), 2, params@w * params@dw, "*")
seal_f_mean    <- rowSums(seal_fmort_mat * biomass_mat) / rowSums(biomass_mat)

m2_mat         <- getM2(params)
m2_mean        <- rowSums(m2_mat * biomass_mat) / rowSums(biomass_mat)

seal_mortality_summary <- data.frame(
  species     = names(seal_f_mean),
  seal_F_mean = round(seal_f_mean, 4),
  M2_mean     = round(m2_mean, 4),
  seal_pct_M2 = round(100 * seal_f_mean / (m2_mean + 1e-10), 1)
) |> arrange(desc(seal_F_mean))

print(seal_mortality_summary)

# Check per-species seal consumption
plotYieldGear(projectToSteady(params, return_sim = TRUE), gears = "Seals")
totalQSeals <- sum(getYieldGear(projectToSteady(params, return_sim = TRUE))[2,"Seals",])

params_steady <- params

```


## Diagnostics: Now check steady state, again
```{r}

# Run the model to steady state and return the full simulation object
# - return_sim = TRUE: keeps the time series data (vs. just returning final params)
# - t_max = 100: allows up to 100 time steps to reach convergence
sim <- steady(params_steady, return_sim = TRUE, t_max = 100)
# Quick plot of total biomass and yields over time (main summary)
plot(sim)

# Check Diagnostic plots
# Plot species biomass over time
# Useful to check if species stabilize or fluctuate at steady state
plotBiomass(sim)

# Plot spectra (biomass by size) from the final state
# Reveals trophic structure and size-based energy flow
plotSpectra(sim)

# Plot species diet composition by size
# Shows who eats whom across size classes
plotDiet(params_steady)

# Plot growth curves for each species
# - species_panel = TRUE: shows separate panels per species
# - max_age = 20: restricts plots to ages up to 20
plotGrowthCurves(params_steady, species_panel = TRUE, max_age = 20)

# Compare model vs observed yield (catch) — seals excluded from model yield
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotYieldExcl(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Compare model vs observed biomass
# - ratio = TRUE: visualizes model/observed ratio; ideal = 1
plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_steady, ratio = TRUE)

# Plot feeding level by size
# Reveals how full each species is at each size (0 = starving, 1 = satiated)
plotFeedingLevel(params_steady)
```

```{r diet-validation-cb}
# Normalise C&B within each predator so fish-prey proportions sum to 1
cb_norm <- cb_raw %>%
  group_by(Predator) %>%
  mutate(cb_prop = pct / sum(pct)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Predator, Prey, cb_prop, source)

# `diet` from the chunk above: Predator, Prey, Ratio (model fish-prey proportions)
diet_compare <- diet %>%
  rename(model_prop = Ratio) %>%
  full_join(cb_norm, by = c("Predator", "Prey")) %>%
  filter(cb_prop > 0.01 | model_prop > 0.01) %>%  # drop negligible entries
  mutate(
    model_prop = replace_na(model_prop, 0),
    cb_prop    = replace_na(cb_prop, 0)
  )

# ── Printed table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("model_prop = mizer emergent; cb_prop = Cook & Bundy (2010) Table 4.1.1\n\n")
diet_compare %>%
  mutate(across(c(model_prop, cb_prop), ~round(., 3)),
         flag = if_else(source == "heuristic", "*", "")) %>%
  arrange(Predator, desc(cb_prop)) %>%
  select(Predator, Prey, model_prop, cb_prop, source) %>%
  print(n = 150)
```

Create size spectrum plots by species with size distribution data from DFO RV Trawl Surveys (q-corrected)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Reshape biomass-at-length to long format (4VsW strata 443-466)
bio_size <- stat |>
  mutate(strat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(STRAT)))) |>
  filter(!is.na(strat_num), strat_num >= 443, strat_num <= 466) |>
  filter(YEAR >= 1978, YEAR <= 1985) |>
  select(Year = YEAR,species_name_raw = COMMON_NAME,
    length_cm = FLEN, Biomass = Biomass_Strata_KG) |>
  mutate(# Herring FLEN is in mm, convert once to cm
    length_cm = ifelse(species_name_raw == "HERRING(ATLANTIC)" & length_cm > 50,length_cm / 10,length_cm),
    Species = species_code_lookup[species_name_raw]) |>
  filter(!is.na(Species)) |> select(Year, Species, length_cm, Biomass)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Check observed length range per species
# ------------------------------------------------------------
max_min_size <- bio_size |>
  group_by(Species) |>
  summarise(min_l = min(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),max_l = max(length_cm, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")

print(max_min_size)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Join L-W parameters and compute weight
# ------------------------------------------------------------
wl <- data.frame(Species = species_params(params_steady)$species,
                 a = species_params(params_steady)$a,b = species_params(params_steady)$b)

bio_size <- bio_size |> left_join(wl, by = "Species") |>
  mutate(  w = a * length_cm ^ b) |> filter(!is.na(Biomass), !is.na(w),w > 0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Bin into weight classes and normalise biomass
# ------------------------------------------------------------
breaks <- 10 ^ seq(0, 6, 0.5)
low    <- head(breaks, -1)
upp    <- tail(breaks, -1)
widths <- upp - low
mid    <- (low + upp) / 2

bio_size <- bio_size |> mutate(bin_id = as.integer(cut(w, breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)),
    weightclass = mid[bin_id],norm_biomass = Biomass / widths[bin_id]) |>
  filter( !is.na(weightclass),!is.na(norm_biomass),is.finite(norm_biomass))

write.csv(bio_size, "Ess_data/bio_size.csv", row.names = FALSE)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Summarise: normalised biomass per weight class x year x species
# ------------------------------------------------------------
biomass_size_spectra <- bio_size |> group_by(weightclass, Year, Species) |>
  summarise(nbiomass = sum(norm_biomass, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop" )

mean_biomass_size_spectra <- biomass_size_spectra |>
  group_by(weightclass, Species) |>
  summarise( mean_nbiomass = mean(nbiomass, na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot: mizer spectra + observed biomass size spectra
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Biomass cutoff lines
# ------------------------------------------------------------
cutoff_lines <- external_species_info |>
  select(Species = species,biomass_cutoff) |> filter(!is.na(biomass_cutoff))

size_distributions <- plotSpectra( params_steady,power = 0,resource = FALSE) +

  # observed spectra
  geom_point(data = mean_biomass_size_spectra,
    aes( x = weightclass,y = mean_nbiomass, colour = Species),inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # biomass cutoff thresholds
  geom_vline(
    data = cutoff_lines, aes(xintercept = biomass_cutoff),
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7,colour = "black",inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Weight class (g)",y = "Normalised mean biomass",
    title = "Observed biomass-at-size compared with mizer spectra",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines indicate biomass cutoff thresholds") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) )

size_distributions
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Calibration_pb_biomass <- plotBiomassObservedVsModel(params_steady, ratio = FALSE, labels = FALSE, return_data = TRUE)

pb_biomass <- mean(1 - Calibration_pb_biomass$ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

Calibration_plot_B <- ggplot(
  Calibration_pb_biomass,
  aes(x = species, y = 1 - ratio, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.3, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colours) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.1) +
  annotate("text",
    x     = length(unique(Calibration_pb_biomass$species)) + 0.5,
    y     = max(1 - Calibration_pb_biomass$ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
    label = expression(bold("(d)")),
    parse = TRUE, size = 3, hjust = 20.5, vjust = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "1 - Modelled/Observed") +
  calibration_theme

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combined plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------
Calibration_plot <- combined_plot / (Calibration_plot_Y + Calibration_plot_B)
Calibration_plot
ggsave(filename = paste0(save_dir, "Calibration_plot.jpeg"), plot = Calibration_plot,
       width = 11,height = 8.5, units = "in",dpi = 400)

Calibration_plot
```

```{r}
names(biomass_sim_base)<-c("Year", "Species","Biomass")


# filter() with no condition does nothing — specify the year range for both
```

Make plots  
plot yields 
```{r}
yield_sim_base <- plotYieldGear(sim, return_data = T) 

# Sum simulated yield across all gears per species per year
yield_sim_total <- yield_sim_base |> group_by(Year, Species) |>
  summarise(Yield_sim = sum(Yield, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Sum fishing only (exclude seals) for comparison to NAFO catches
yield_sim_fishing <- yield_sim_base |>
  filter(Gear != "Seals") |>
  group_by(Year, Species) |>
  summarise(Yield_fishing = sum(Yield, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Plot fishing yield vs observed
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = filter(yield_sim_fishing, !Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")),aes(x = Year, y = Yield_fishing / 1e9), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = filter(yield_ts,!Species %in% c("Sand Lance", "Capelin", "Longhorn Sculpin")),
             aes(x = Year, y = Yield / 1e9), size = 0.8, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Yield (thousand tonnes)",
       title = "Model fishing yield (blue) vs observed NAFO catches (red)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8)

```

Creating a data frame of constant fishing (mean fishing) with extra effort (Seals)
```{r}
fishing_history = read.csv("Ess_data/effort_gear_with_seals.csv",row.names = 1)
effort<-fishing_history[as.character("1978":"2024"),]
effort_with_seal <- as.matrix(effort)

# Add Year column from row names
effort$Year <- as.numeric(rownames(effort))
# Convert to long format
effort_long <- effort %>%pivot_longer(cols = -Year, names_to = "Gear",values_to = "Effort" )
# Rename for publication-style labels
effort_long$Gear <- factor(
  effort_long$Gear,
  levels = c("Bottom_Trawl", "Fixed_Gear", "Pelagic", "Small_Mesh", "Seals"),
  labels = c("Bottom trawl", "Fixed gear", "Pelagic","Small mesh", "Grey seals"))
# facet plot
p <- ggplot(effort_long, aes(x = Year, y = Effort)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ Gear, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020),
    labels = c("1980", "1990", "2000", "2010", "2020"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative effort (0–1)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    strip.text        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.text         = element_text(colour = "black", size = 9),
    axis.line         = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks        = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.spacing.x   = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    panel.spacing.y   = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    plot.margin       = margin(10, 15, 8, 10)
  )
p

#save effort forcing matrix object for later use
```
